history.caption: When a schema demands the answer field before the reasoning field, the model generates an output without the computational space to process the steps.
history.title: Agentic AI Schema Ordering

style_when: the story is a single number, rule, gate or shift and restraint is the point — with no scene to photograph, the frame must still be a real assembly: a modular bay, an unlatched inspection gate, a rack of blades, an interlocking connector
prompt: Minimalist studio composition of a modular mechanical assembly on a weathered concrete surface. Three sequential precision-engineered processing modules are abruptly blocked by a heavy, latched polished metal output casing placed prematurely at the front of the sequence. Asymmetric off-centre framing, generous negative space on the right. Hard clean edges, one stark directional light throwing long cast shadows across the concrete. Matte muted palette with industrial greys and a single warm copper accent on the blocked modules. No bare shapes, no molded or printed lettering.
negative_prompt: garbled text, random lettering, watermarks, typography, UI elements, labels
rationale: The story is about how structural ordering and rigid schema sequences dictate a systemic process. A minimalist component assembly captures this by arranging recognizable engineered modules to show an inverted sequence.
cue: put the working field before the answer field
subject: an engineered modular assembly with a dominant final output block placed prematurely before sequential processing modules
core_thesis: A tool schema dictates token-by-token generation order, and forcing the answer field before the reasoning field causes models to skip the work and lose massive accuracy.
core_conflict: Premature output generation versus step-by-step reasoning sequence.
